newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduran church blasted for halting condom giveaway.
newsitem.headline: Honduran church blasted for halting condom giveaway.

text.p: A top Honduran health official on Thursday blasted the local Roman Catholic Church for using its influence to stop a plan to hand out condoms at polling stations during Sunday's primary elections.

Health and elections officials had planned to distribute more than one million condoms at polling stations on Sunday when Hondurans belonging to the two major parties vote to choose candidates for president and other offices.
Officials said Wednesday the plan had been cancelled largely because of opposition from the church.
Honduras has the worst AIDS problem in Central America with 8,300 reported cases and 1,032 deaths registered since 1985.

"The Honduran population continues having sexual relations outside marriage and these institutions that supposedly have centuries promoting this (fidelity) have not had any impact," Enrique Zelaya, the vice minister of health, told reporters.
The Catholic Church long has opposed condoms as a means of slowing the spread of AIDS, saying condoms promote promiscuity, and instead favours abstinence and marital fidelity.

"I think that continuing with the attitude of wanting to block out the sun with a finger doesn't help at all in the fight against this evil (AIDS)," Zelaya said, using a popular Central American refrain.
